title: Batching-aware cache policy synthesis and chaos-tested rollback runbook
creator: Marcus Rivera
description: Goal: Produce an automated policy generator that recommends KV/prefix cache key designs, TTL schedules, and batching-aware cache configuration bundles, plus a tested rollback/runbook so we can apply changes with low risk and fast recovery. This ticket covers modeling, simulator integration, recommendation API, staged rollout orchestration, and a documented rollback playbook. The output should be a config bundle that can be applied via CI and rolled back automatically if safety gates trip.
background: We have recurring manual tuning requests where teams adjust TTLs and cache keys to balance cost and latency. Current heuristics ignore batching profiles, leading to suboptimal unit economics when request batching shifts under load. Existing work on prefix and TTL autotuning focuses on hit-rate curves but does not synthesize end-to-end bundles that include batching-aware knobs or a deterministic rollback path. This work will bridge batching behavior into policy synthesis and formalize a chaos-tested rollback runbook.
approach: Instrument request traces to capture per-route batching profile: batch size distribution, inter-arrival times, and token lengths (privacy-safe sample).

Build a Monte Carlo ensemble hit-rate simulator that consumes: prefix frequency sketches, batch profiles, and candidate cache key transformations to estimate hit-rate and per-token cost across workload percentiles.
Create TTL annealing schedules (gradual TTL shrink/expansion) driven by modeled cost/latency tradeoff curves; represent schedules as time-windowed change-sets compatible with the config API.
Synthesize candidate cache key transforms (composite-key templates, affix trimming, suffix hashing) and score them by projected cost delta and hit-rate stability under workload perturbations.
Expose a recommendations API that returns ranked config bundles with confidence bands and suggested canary parameters: shadowing fraction, canary routes, and time windows.
Implement orchestrator adapters: GitOps/CICD patcher that can apply bundle and create a rollback changelist tied to the deployment artifact.
Develop automated safety gates that monitor cost delta, 95th p99 latency, and generation quality regressions (via eval prompts). Gates trigger immediate rollback when breached.
Run systematic chaos tests in staging that exercise high variance traffic, delayed KV responses, and evictions to validate rollback latency and false-positive rates.
Ship a runbook with exact play commands, dashboard links, and escalation steps for on-call engineers and SREs.
simulator_plan: Create a corpus of representative traffic snapshots (synthetic and sampled production traces with PII redaction). The simulator runs 1000 Monte Carlo trials per candidate bundle across workload perturbations (±20% QPS, burst patterns, and shifted batch size distributions). Output metrics: expected tokens saved per 1M requests, median/p99 generation latency delta, and probability of cache thrash (eviction-induced miss storms). Use these outputs to compute an expected utility score and a conservatism-adjusted recommendation rank.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Offline evaluation and PR with recommendation bundle + simulator results. Invite PM and Design for review of quality impacts.
Step 1: Canary apply at 1% traffic with shadowing enabled for 24h; collect cost/latency/quality signals.
Step 2: If gates pass, ramp to 10% for 2h, then 30% for 4h. At each step, run automated evaluation against the held prompt suite.
Step 3: Full apply with rolling waves (60->100%) only if all acceptance criteria satisfied for 24h at 30% and 4h at 60%.
Rollback: automated rollback triggers on gate failure; manual rollback steps included in runbook for on-call. Aim for rollback completion <5 minutes from trigger to observed traffic change.
acceptance_criteria: Projected median per-token cost decreases by >= 8% on target routes in simulator at expected traffic distribution.
No more than 1% absolute increase in p99 generation latency during canary (measured over 10k samples).
End-to-end rollout completes with automated rollback tested in staging and rollback time measured <5 minutes.
Quality regressions on the canonical prompt suite are <= 0.5% relative to baseline and flagged in the PR.
Recommendation API surfaces confidence bands and expected cost/latency deltas for each bundle.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Simulator mismatch to production leading to mis-ranked bundles. Mitigation: conservative scoring (discounting expected savings by uncertainty), continuous shadow validation, and phased ramping.
Risk: Overaggressive TTL shrink causing cache churn and increased backend load. Mitigation: TTL annealing with guardrails, eviction-rate monitors, and immediate rollback triggers.

Risk: Regression in output quality not caught by small eval suite. Mitigation: expand prompt coverage, use stratified samples by customer/route, and require PM/design signoff for quality-sensitive routes.
Risk: Rollback automation does not complete under partial control-plane outage. Mitigation: include manual CLI steps in runbook with pre-approved rollback artifacts and runbook owner on pager.
